name: Tharnu
myth: In the thaw, when the sea goes grey and the floes grind like teeth, the boats stay tied under the cliffs. Ennu the Kite-Wright sat too long over her cloth one spring and forgot the boats. Orrun felt the ice on his back and rolled, and the floes broke open in a line. Ennu saw the black water and was ashamed. She took a long oar of bone and pushed a boat out through the gap. Nobody on the cliffs saw her face, only the stroke. Tavo came down the wind to laugh at her, and she did not look up. The stroke went on until the ice lay open from the cliffs to the far skerries. Then she hung the oar in the Upper Sea, so the people would know where the water had given way. Her hands are still on it. In spring, watch for the pale line, and when you see it, mend your own boats.
verse:
Ennu's oar goes through
the floes where cold sea opened
pale line in the spring
